We graded Bot On Deck on the same five dimensions as every review on this site: ease of use, features, transparency, security and support. The number below is ours, and the evidence sits in the sections above it.
whatItClaims: Around-the-clock support through the partner desk.
Signals generated without manual chart reading.
A US$250 minimum deposit to start.
Free registration, with account activation by confirmation link.
Risk settings adjustable before the first live trade.
whatWeChecked: The number reuse: one score figure doing more than one job.
The deposit terms: minimum amount, payment methods and where the money sits.
The demo claim: practice account confirmed in the signup flow.
The payout promise: within-a-day wording without processing detail.
The broker relationship: which partner desk executes orders.
The asset list: how many pairs are actually offered.

steps.title: Register
steps.text: Provide your details on the signup page and confirm the account through the link you receive.

steps.title: Fund
steps.text: Fund the account with US$250 - bank cards, transfer, PayPal and Skrill are accepted.

steps.title: Configure
steps.text: Set your preferences, select automatic or manual execution, and run the practice account first.

pros: No platform fees on top of spreads.
cons: Marketing numbers that the fine print walks back.
redFlags: Payout promises with no processing detail.
No regulator, licence or audit named anywhere.
Marketing numbers the fine print quietly qualifies.

faqs.q: Is it really fee-free?
faqs.a: The platform fee is absent, but every trade carries a broker spread the page itself calls the real cost. The headline says free; the fine print says otherwise. Budget for the fine print.

faqs.q: Is Bot On Deck safe, legit or a scam?
faqs.a: We found no scam indicators in the product, which reads as a functioning AI trading service. The conditions are editorial: claims without verification, conflicting figures and restriction lists that disagree. We rate it safe to research with the conditions in this review.

faqs.q: How much support does it offer?
faqs.a: Unclear - around-the-clock coverage is claimed, while other sections quote different figures. Ask support to reconcile them before you fund anything.

faqs.q: What happens after I sign up?
faqs.a: You confirm the account by email, fund US$250, set your risk preferences and choose automatic or manual mode. The demo account runs alongside while you learn.

faqs.q: Where is Bot On Deck restricted?
faqs.a: The lists conflict - different sections of the site name different countries. Confirm your eligibility with support before depositing.

bottomLine: The verdict on the product is cautious approval: it works, it includes a demo, and it should be used with the minimum deposit while the claims are unproven.
Our 4.2 reflects what the pages publish and what they skip. It is not a warning off - it is a reminder to trade the product, not the pitch.
